land.text: Bali: Majapahit 'captured the Balinese capital of Bedulu in 1343' and gave authority over Bali to Arya Damar's younger brothers

successors.note: The Bali Kingdom page's infobox has a Majapahit vassal phase 1343-1478, then the Gelgel Kingdom (1478-1661): Cliopatria's later rows 'Balinese Kingdom' (1519-1686) and 'Bali' (1687-1907) are the same page. Cliopatria's Majapahit shape holds the island from 1344. Whether they are the same state is for the colour agent; they are separate dossiers (se-02-e).

capitals.name: Bedulu
capitals.note: Infobox capitals: 'Bedulu (Warmadewa period)', Samprangan (Majapahit period), Gelgel, Klungkung; no years are given. The page does not name Singhamandawa or Pejeng as capitals; Majapahit 'captured the Balinese capital of Bedulu in 1343'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 922; the page's infobox has 'Sovereign state (914-1343)' and the Belanjong pillar of Sri Kesari Warmadewa is 'dated 914 CE according to the Indian Saka calendar' (infobox '13 or 27 February 914'). The shape is Cliopatria's 922 shape unchanged.
7,748 km2 for 922-1009: the island of Bali with its offshore islands (bbox 114.3-115.6E, 8.1-8.9S). The page gives no area or extent for the Warmadewa kingdom beyond the island; nothing to compare.

correction.text: Bali under its own kings, with Mataram (to 1016) and then Airlangga's Kahuripan as probable suzerains: Cliopatria's 922 shape held from 1010

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1010-1045: Cliopatria has no Early Balinese shape, and its Kahuripan shape of 1028-1045 holds the whole island (22 cells), with nothing for Bali in 1010-1027. Airlangga was born in Bali c. 1002; his father Udayana was a Balinese king of the Warmadewa dynasty; Marakata became king of Bali after Udayana and Anak Wungcu after Marakata, so Bali kept its own kings. The page says Bali 'probably was an ally or vassal of Java' and that Airlangga 'extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali'. The shape is the 922 shape unchanged.

7,719 km2 for 1046-1235, the same island. The Kediri page, citing the Chu-fan-chi (c. 1225), lists Bali ('Ma-li') among the colonies of the Javanese maharaja and does not say whether it was vassal, ally or independent; the Bali page keeps it sovereign (914-1343).

correction.text: Bali until Kertanegara's expedition of 1284: Cliopatria's 1046 shape held from 1236

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1236-1283, which Cliopatria leaves empty (neither its Kediri nor its Singhasari shape holds a Bali cell): no page opened ends Balinese rule in 1236 (Singhasari's Ken Arok took Kediri in 1222), and the 1284 'hostile Pabali expedition to Bali' of Kertanegara presupposes a Bali not yet Singhasari's. The shape is the 1046 shape unchanged.

correction.text: Bali again its own kingdom after Singhasari's fall in 1292: the shape unchanged, held 1293-1332 only

keyframe_review.note: 7,719 km2 for 1285-1332. Kertanegara 'led a hostile Pabali expedition to Bali' in 1284 and, on both the Singhasari and Bali pages, 'integrated Bali into the Singhasari kingdom's territory'; Singhasari fell to Jayakatwang in 1292, and the Majapahit page's conquest of the Balinese king at Bedulu in 1343 shows Bali sovereign again by then. So the shape holds from 1293, not 1285; for 1284-1292 the island is Singhasari's. The shape is unchanged.

7,719 km2 for 1333-1343, identical to 1285; Cliopatria's split at 1333 has no page behind it (the Majapahit page gives the Palapa oath as 1334 or 1336). Majapahit's forces came in 1342 and 'captured the Balinese capital of Bedulu in 1343'.

ledger.note: 914: Sri Kesari Warmadewa raises the Belanjong pillar on Bali. 'Sovereign state (914-1343)'; the pillar is 'dated 914 CE according to the Indian Saka calendar' (infobox 13 or 27 February 914); the Warmadewa line ruled from Bedulu. The page gives the date, not the extent: the island is the reading.

1284: Kertanegara of Singhasari invades Bali. He 'led a hostile Pabali expedition to Bali', which 'integrated Bali into the Singhasari kingdom's territory'; the Bali page: the expedition 'seems to have integrated Bali into Singhasari's realm'. Neither page says a Balinese king was captured.
c. 1293: Bali is its own kingdom again (page silent on the year). Singhasari fell to Jayakatwang in 1292 and Majapahit was founded in 1293; the Majapahit page finds a Balinese king at Bedulu in 1342.

region.text: Bali island, fought over for seven months

ledger.note: 1342: Majapahit lands on Bali. 'in 1342, Majapahit forces led by Gajah Mada and assisted by General Arya Damar' (per the Babad Arya Tabanan); 'After seven months of battles' the Balinese king was beaten.
1343: Bedulu falls. 'After seven months of battles, Majapahit defeated the Balinese king and captured the Balinese capital of Bedulu in 1343.'

1343: Bali becomes Majapahit's. Majapahit gave authority over Bali to Arya Damar's younger brothers; the Bali page's infobox has a Majapahit vassal phase 1343-1478 (the page's 'Samprangan' dynasty under Sri Aji Kresna Kepakisan, c. 1352 in the infobox).

region.text: Bali, the last Early Balinese shape

ledger.note: 1343: the sovereign Bali kingdom ends. The infobox's 'Sovereign state (914-1343)' is followed by 'Majapahit vassal (1343-1478)'; 'Majapahit forces, led by Gajah Mada, defeated the Balinese king at Bedulu', landing in 1342 and winning in 1343.

wars.name: Singhasari expedition to Bali
wars.outcome: Bali integrated into Singhasari's realm; neither page says for how long, the Majapahit page finding a sovereign Balinese king in 1342.
wars.note: The Singhasari page calls it 'a hostile Pabali expedition' in 1284; the Bali page: 'seems to have integrated Bali'.

wars.name: Majapahit conquest of Bali
wars.outcome: Majapahit wins after seven months and captures Bedulu in 1343; authority over Bali goes to Arya Damar's younger brothers.
wars.note: The Bali page has the troops landing in 1342 and winning in 1343 under Gajah Mada; the Majapahit page does not name the Balinese king.

certainty.note: The island's coast fixes the land, but the pages give no frontier and the extent beyond Bali (Lombok, Nusa Penida) is not described before the Gelgel period.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Early Balinese Kingdoms' (922-1343) shares Wikipedia 'Bali Kingdom' and Wikidata Q12491027 with 'Balinese Kingdom' (1519-1686) and 'Bali' (1687-1907). Kept here as the pre-Majapahit sovereign kingdom (infobox 914-1343) only; the Gelgel and Klungkung rows belong to another dossier (se-02-e). Between 1343 and 1478 the page has Bali a Majapahit vassal and Cliopatria has no Bali shape until 1519; the three rows could be one state with a vassal phase, which the colour agent should decide (all three are family southeast-asia). Majapahit's own dossier should carry Bali as vassal or province from 1343. Start 914 (infobox, Belanjong pillar) against Cliopatria's 922. Cliopatria's gaps 1010-1045 and 1236-1284 are bridged by new keyframes (the pages show Bali under its own kings, Marakata and Anak Wungcu, and an unsubdued Bali before 1284); the 1285 shape is cut to 1293-1332 because both the Singhasari and Bali pages say Kertanegara integrated Bali in 1284. Bali as Mataram or Kahuripan vassal in the 11th century ('probably') and as Kediri's colony c. 1225 (Chu-fan-chi) are carried in those states' dossiers, not here. The Warmadewa line, Udayana, Airlangga's brothers and Jayapangus (1178-81) are on the page without reign dates, so no ruler strip. No infobox area. Counterpart without dossier: none new.
